page: Amazon Web Services c8ine.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by high-frequency Intel x86_64 processors. It provides 32 vCPUs derived from 16 dedicated physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds reaching 3.9 GHz. System memory is provisioned at 64.0 GB, maintaining a compute-aligned memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual processor.

The hardware configuration does not include local instance storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote elastic block storage. Networking is a primary feature of this instance class, delivering a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. This combination offers high per-thread execution speed paired with significant ingress and egress capacity, making it suited for bandwidth-intensive distributed computing.

Workloads best aligned with the c8ine.8xlarge include compute-heavy network applications, distributed analytics nodes, continuous integration pipelines, batch rendering, and compute-bound microservices that require rapid packet throughput without needing large pools of memory or local high-speed NVMe storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c8ine.8xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 cloud server powered by 3.9 GHz dedicated Intel processors on the AWS Nitro System. Configured with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 64.0 GB of system RAM, it maintains a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation focused on compute-bound execution. The instance features a substantial 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating high-throughput data movement across distributed nodes. It includes no local storage or hardware accelerators, relying on external network-attached volumes for persistent data. This profile is well suited for compute-intensive network appliances, distributed processing engines, web cluster backends, and batch compilation pipelines.
